correctness.rationale: From the displayed Betz–Fu–Masuda regularized boundary equations, c(r)=(au+brv)/(a+br) and logit(r)=beta[d+h c(r)] are equivalent for every physical candidate. The derivative numerator has exact discriminant K[K-4a(a+b)], so the one/two/three root counts, folds, and environmental stability signs follow by monotonic intervals. Exact rational witness gives c(1/2)=13/19, F(1/2)=0, F'(1/2)=-1836/361 and distinct outer roots on opposite sides of 1/2; the invariant-boundary environment eigenvalue at the midpoint is 459/475. The included standard-library checker validates exact arithmetic and tests numerical root brackets. The limitation to a formal boundary approximation is explicit.

value.rationale: The 2026 source leaves open how many rare-cooperator boundary candidate solutions its practical approximation can produce. A sharp universal parameter threshold, complete one/two/three multiplicity regime, and admissible opposing-invasion-sign witness make the interpretation of boundary stability tests precise. This directly motivated classification of a physically derived criterion is more informative than a routine evaluation at fixed parameters, while limits of the boundary approximation are stated.
